as_of_semantics.conflicts: if several providers disagree the most severe visible state is returned with conflict=true; nothing is averaged or invented
as_of_semantics.no_record: UNKNOWN with reason NO_VISIBLE_RECORD; absence is never read as ACTIVE
as_of_semantics.visibility: a record is visible only if published_at <= cutoff AND retrieved_at <= cutoff (when the source gives no published_at the retrieval time is the knowledge time), valid_from <= cutoff, valid_to is null or cutoff < valid_to, not postgame (retrieved at or after kickoff), not (backfilled and not original_vintage), and its cutoff_eligibility covers the requested label. Among visible revisions of one source record the highest revision_sequence wins. A later update can never leak backward: QUESTIONABLE at T24 followed by OUT at T90 stays QUESTIONABLE at T24 and OUT at T90.

identity: exact (game_id, player_id) with GSIS ids; never name matching; a record without a GSIS id is rejected

link_to_phase2a.never: Phase2B never writes to, edits or re-hashes a Phase2A ledger or the Phase2A lock
questions: roster ACT but officially inactive (needs an accepted injury source)?
status changed between T24 and T90?

no_go: no Week5+ outcome access (availability records carry no outcomes)
no production, frontend, scheduler or other-sport change
no systematic retrieval of NFL.com or team pages (terms prohibit it without written consent)

operator_aid.rule: read-only: it never creates a forecast, a capture or any file; no clock override exists in the CLI

preregistration: Committed before any Phase2B record exists. DATA CAPTURE / MEASUREMENT ONLY. Phase2A engine v1.0 stays frozen: Phase2B never alters a Phase2A forecast, eligibility rule, ledger row, comparator row or the engine lock. Availability rows are separate observational records linked by game_id, player_id and cutoff_type. Whether availability should enter a forecast is a separate, later, preregistered phase after enough forward records exist.

qb.rule: QB-state records are NOT duplicated. Any QB starter / health provider payload is routed through nfl_v2_qb_state_ingestion.ingest_qb_state, state_at and certify_for_forecast (Phase1M schema). The roster-status observation of a QB is only a roster-status availability row flagged ROSTER_STATUS_ONLY_NOT_A_QB_STATE. No real QB source is certified unless it passes the existing acceptance harness.

question: Can a timestamp-valid forward archive of offensive-player availability information at T24 and T90 be built without historical backfill or leakage?

sources.rule: only legitimately capturable sources; no unauthorized scraper; "publicly viewable" does not mean systematic collection is permitted. Classifications: ACCEPTED_FORWARD_CAPTURE, PROMISING_NEEDS_TERMS, PROMISING_NEEDS_ACCESS, BLOCKED_LICENSE, BLOCKED_TIMING, NOT_USEFUL. A source is usable only if phase2b_source_acceptance.json classifies it ACCEPTED_FORWARD_CAPTURE and the record fields stay inside its accepted scope; the code refuses everything else.

storage.empty_until_real: nothing is populated with invented data; fixtures are labelled FIXTURE_ONLY_NOT_REAL_AVAILABILITY_EVIDENCE and live only in tests
storage.format: hash-chained append-only JSONL (same primitives as the Phase2A ledgers); existing lines are never rewritten; a revision is a new row with a higher revision_sequence; identical content re-seen is not a revision

measures: MAE by ACTIVE-like / QUESTIONABLE / DOUBTFUL / OUT-INACTIVE / UNKNOWN

catastrophic Phase2A misses (receiving yards > 40, rushing yards > 30, targets > 4, carries > 8, receptions > 3) associated with a status downgrade, a late inactive, or an incomplete availability state
value_report.populations: identical player-games; unlinked forecasts reported separately as UNLINKED
value_report.when: only after games are graded by the frozen Phase2A grader

windows.late: a capture attempt after a cutoff is logged MISSED_CAPTURE for that game, cutoff and provider; it is never backfilled or relabelled as timely
windows.rule: exactly the Phase2A windows (nfl_v2_phase2a_forward_forecast.window / classify; no new timing protocol)
